name: Brazzaville
subtitle: Brazzaville, capital of the Republic of the Congo: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,138,236 people lived in the Commune of Brazzaville in the official May 2023 census (RGPH-5).
Situated on the Pool Malebo, Brazzaville directly faces Kinshasa across the Congo River, forming the closest pair of sovereign capitals in the world.
During World War II, Brazzaville served as the official wartime capital of Free France under Félix Éboué and Charles de Gaulle.

parts.text: Brazzaville was founded in September 1880 when naval officer Pietro Savorgnan di Brazzà concluded a protectorate treaty with King Illoy I (Makoko of Mbé), paramount ruler of the Bateke kingdom, on the northern bank of the Pool Malebo.

Between 1910 and 1958, Brazzaville served as the federal capital of French Equatorial Africa (AEF) and notably became the capital of Free France (France Libre) from 1940 to 1943 during the Second World War.

Following national independence in August 1960, the city emerged as a vibrant center of African arts, fashion, and intellectual life, home to the celebrated painters of Poto-Poto and the iconic elegance movement of the Sapeurs.
